dedupe_keys.name: raabit recovery assessment using agent based tools post wildfire housing recovery model

description: RAAbIT, Recovery Assessment using Agent-based Tools, is an agent-based model of post-disaster housing recovery designed to run on data available within weeks of an event. Households, insurers and contractors are agents following empirical behaviour rules, and system constraints such as contractor availability can be changed to reflect local conditions. Rodrigo Costa of the University of Waterloo, Ali Nejat of Texas Tech University and Sara Hamideh of Stony Brook University published it in Scientific Reports in June 2026, hindcasting the 2017 Tubbs Fire in Santa Rosa and the 2018 Camp Fire in Paradise, where 57 percent and 9 percent of destroyed homes were rebuilt within five years; the model reproduces the temporal and spatial patterns seen in permit and construction data. Coverage is the two California cases, with a transferable design. Format and access: code and replication data deposited on Zenodo, with an open access paper. Licence: the article is CC-BY-4.0, and the code licence was not read because the Zenodo record could not be opened. Caveats: validation covers two wildfires only. It supports agent-based resilience and recovery planning after disasters. Related catalogue records are the 2018 Camp Fire evacuation case and the NIST WUI fire structure and parcel case studies.
